newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico presents fresh evidence in assassination.
newsitem.headline: Mexico presents fresh evidence in assassination.

text.p: Mexican prosecutors said on Wednesday they had fresh murder evidence against Raul Salinas, the brother of disgraced former president Carlos Salinas.

Jose Luis Ramos Rivera, the prosecutor in charge of the murder case, told reporters his team had shown a judge 16 new pieces of evidence against Raul Salinas, some of which he said had been deliberately suppressed by previous investigators. Raul Salinas is accused of ordering a high-level political assassination.

The testimony "strengthens the exercise of penal action" against Salinas for allegedly ordering the 1994 shooting of Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, the No. 2 official in the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party, he added.

Salinas was arrested in February 1995 and accused of masterminding the murder of Ruiz Massieu, supposedly because of a personal vendetta. Ruiz Massieu was divorced from Raul's sister Adriana at the time of the killing.
Prosecutors also charged Salinas with illicit enrichment after finding more than $100 million he stashed away in various foreign bank accounts.

Salinas has denied all the charges against him and the murder investigation ran into trouble at the start of this year when authorities said prosecutors had faked evidence to try to incriminate Salinas.

Among the fresh evidence, Ramos played a portion of a cassette tape anonymously sent to prosecutors, who are keen to dispel the impression that the government might be preparing to abandon the politically sensitive case against Salinas.

The tape purportedly records part of an interrogation of Jorge Rodriguez Gonzalez, one of a pair of brothers accused of hiring the contract killer who gunned down Ruiz Massieu outside a Mexico City hotel.
In the tape, a voice identified by authorities as that of Rodriguez is heard saying that his brother and alleged co-conspirator Fernando told him that Raul Salinas had ordered the murder.
"Raul Salinas told him to eliminate Mr. Ruiz Massieu," the voice identified as Rodriguez said in the tape.

In another piece of evidence, former attorney-general Victor Humberto Benitez testified that Salinas had approached him one day at the presidential palace and expressed concern that he might be linked to the Ruiz Massieu murder probe.

Ramos said the new evidence showed that previous investigators of the murder "diverted the course of the investigations because although testimony was obtained linking Raul Salinas de Gortari in the murder, mention of this was eliminated from the investigation".
Ramos did not address the issue of Raul's alleged illicit enrichment during the news conference.
After reading a prepared statement about the murder investigation against the former president's brother, he left hastily without taking questions.
